raw:
The foyer is cooler now, the front doors dark panes against Harbour Street. You fill a clean glass at the kitchen tap while Jo dries the last of the serving spoons.

“Help yourself,” she says. “There’ll be tea in the morning, once I’ve found where they’ve hidden the decent mugs.”

Back in the foyer, Rosa is packing her camera into its padded case. Martin and Owen carry the final programme board from the auditorium and ease it against the side wall with the others. Bea checks the row without touching the painted surfaces.

“Blue board’s all right?” she asks.

“I’ve got it,” Rosa says. “Close-ups as well as the full thing.”

Martin nods toward the board. “It’s meant to look worn. Don’t let anybody clean the history off it.”

“That is, more or less, the plan.”

The office is dark and shut; Nell has apparently left. Above, a brief metallic click travels down from the projection booth, followed by Dev moving around overhead.

At twenty to eight, Bea puts on her coat. Rosa thanks Martin for his notes, and Owen offers to help her carry the camera case out to the lane. Jo begins tying up a bag of leftover bread for herself.

You stand with your water near the café tables as the small group finishes folding itself out of the evening.
